candidate.note: A planet candidate from an automated search, not a confirmed planet. It needs review by people and follow-up observations; other things, such as a faint background binary, can look the same.

checks.name: snr
checks.reason: The dip stands 55 times above the noise over 40 events.

checks.name: odd_even
checks.reason: Alternate dips have matching depths (0.079% vs 0.079%), as expected for a planet.

checks.name: secondary_eclipse
checks.reason: Halfway round the orbit there is no significant dip, consistent with a planet.

checks.name: size
checks.reason: Dip depth 0.079% on a 3.23 R_sun star implies about 0.88 Jupiter radii (9.9 Earth radii), likely range 0.85-0.91. That is within the size range of planets.

checks.name: period_alias
checks.reason: The period holds up against P/2, 2P and 3P: P/2: dip at half phase -2% of the main one; 2P: shallowest group 99% of the rest; 3P: shallowest group 97% of the rest.

checks.name: momentum_dump
checks.reason: 0 of 40 dips coincide with a momentum dump and 1 more with quality-flagged cadences; the clean dips alone are 100% as deep as all of them, so the signal does not come from spacecraft events.

checks.name: sector_depth
checks.reason: The dip depth agrees between sectors (S81 796±37, S82 794±33, S83 731±36 ppm; chance of this scatter 0.34).

checks.name: duration
checks.reason: The dip lasts 1.9 h; a planet crossing the middle of this star (density 0.07 solar, from TIC density) on a 1.775-day orbit would take about 5.6 h, so the length fits.

checks.name: single_sector
checks.reason: Not a single-sector signal: dips were seen in 3 sectors.

score_detail.formula: (0.40*S_snr + 0.20*S_transits + 0.25*S_checks + 0.15*S_brightness) * (0.8 if single-sector); each part = weight * S * factor

stand_in.name: TOI-1364.01
stand_in.note: This is TOI-1364.01, already a TESS Object of Interest (ExoFOP disposition PC). The live search would file it as already known; it is shown here as a stand-in because the 2026-09-26 search found no new candidate.
